concept.name: Total supply
concept.definition: Total supply is the total number of tokens that have been created (minted) so far, minus any that have been verifiably burned — i.e. all tokens in existence whether or not they are circulating.
concept.intuition: It is the full headcount of minted tokens: circulating plus everything still locked in vesting contracts, treasuries and escrow.
concept.mechanics: Total supply = cumulative issuance − cumulative burns; it grows with emissions (block rewards, unlock-related mints) and shrinks with burns (e.g. EIP-1559 base-fee burning on Ethereum). Locked/vested tokens count toward total supply but not circulating supply, so total ≥ circulating at any moment.
concept.formula: Total supply = Σ minted − Σ burned; Circulating supply ≤ Total supply ≤ Maximum supply.
concept.failure_modes: Projects blur total vs circulating to make valuations look smaller or larger as convenient; tokens in 'ecosystem' wallets technically count as total supply while being economically equivalent to insider float.
concept.misconceptions: Total supply is not the cap — for inflationary tokens there is no maximum, and total supply grows indefinitely. A low total supply number means nothing for price without knowing emission rate and burns.
concept.example: Ethereum's total supply equals all ETH ever issued as block rewards minus all ETH burned via base fees since EIP-1559 — fluctuating near ~120M with no maximum cap.
